klaudia: Quick sync: execs asked for an 'isolation maturity model' so customers can see clear upgrade paths, expected lead times, and gated launch criteria. Need to pick a canonical taxonomy.

omar: Love that. My vote: use four tiers not three. Tier 0: shared-hosted (baseline). Tier 1: residency-enabled (region pin + platform KMS). Tier 2: soft-slices (reservation + QoS + partial SLA). Tier 3: hard-islands (physical isolation + customer CMK + extended retention). Each tier should have expected timeframe, infra delta, and commercial multiplier.

ben: Ops input: for tiers 2/3 we must list scheduler features precisely: reservation API, preemption policy, cross-az placement controls. Otherwise we undercommit and cause noisy neighbor incidents.

tess: Product request: include policy composability rules. For example, residency should always win over cost-based fallback. We need a decision on policy precedence and how multiple predicates combine.

faiz: Security/legal note: islands require legal DPIA sign-off for EU financials and a validated key lifecycle plan. Add 'legal review' as a mandatory gate for Tier 3.

klaudia: Example snippet for policy DSL in the doc: `policies: [ {name: "residency", predicate: "region == 'eu'", action: {route: "eu-pool", lock: true}}, {name: "slice", predicate: "tenant.slice == 'gold'", action: {reserve: 2, fallback: "shared"}} ]`. We'll call out how precedence is resolved (explicit priority array).

omar: Timeline suggestion: Tier 0->1 (hosted residency + platform KMS) = 4w. Tier 1->2 (slice primitives + telemetry + billing) = 8-10w. Tier 2->3 (physical isolation, ops-certifications) = 12-16w. These are parallelizable but require scheduler + infra ops involvement.

ben: Telemetry requirement: every request MUST emit `route_reason` and `route_hash`. For islands add `isolation_id`. Retention for Tier3 should be configurable up to 3 years.

tess: Launch gates per tier (proposed): Tier1: residency verification, KMS rotate test, 2 canaries. Tier2: perf cert, quota dashboard, chaos test for noisy neighbor, billing integration. Tier3: legal DPIA, on-prem runbook, dedicated SRE rota, 3 canaries.

faiz: Commercial note: customers will ask for deterministic failover semantics. For Tier2 default should be auto-fallback to shared if slice overloaded unless customer opts out. For Tier3 the default must be no automatic fallback. Document this clearly.

klaudia: Risk register: call out three high risks: (1) scheduler reservation starvation, (2) telemetry cardinality from per-tenant traces, (3) legal delays for islands. Include mitigations.

omar: Cost model ask: finance wants a simple formula. Proposal: baseline cost C; Tier1 = C * 1.15, Tier2 = C * 1.9, Tier3 = C * 3.6. We'll flag as draft and ask finance to validate.

ben: Ops implementation notes: reservation API needs metrics: reserved_vcpu, reserved_gpu, reservation_utilization. Add per-tenant admission rejection reasons to logs for easier debugging.

tess: Product action: I'll author the one-pager with maturity matrix, policy precedence rules, sample DSL, gating checklist, and a slide for sales. Will link to RFC for infra.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: created ticket ISOMODE-900 "isolation-maturity-model + policy-composability RFC" assigned ben. Link: https://redwood.atlassian/ISOMODE-900

faiz: Action items: Ben -> technical RFC + scheduler constraints; Omar -> timeline + cost-band proposal; Tess -> one-pager + sales slide; Klaudia -> coordinate legal signoff path for Tier3. Target alignment in roadmap review (ts 3971234100).

klaudia: One more thing: include a small 'rollback playbook' for each tier. Customers will want to know how we revert a migration safely (data dual-write window, canary rollback, credit calculation). Add that to gates.

omar: Agreed. I'll add a short rollback appendix to the RFC.

ben: Will start RFC today. Expect draft in product/rfc/isolation-maturity by EOD.

tess: I'll ping here when the one-pager is ready. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
